title: Fonterra Shareholders' Fund stock gets stronger milk outlook
summary: 新西兰农场的股东基金因牛奶前景向好而表现强劲，反映出全球乳业市场对原料供应的积极预期。这一趋势对跨境奶粉供应链的稳定性和成本控制具有重要影响，从业者需关注国际乳业动态，优化采购和物流策略。
points: 新西兰农场的股东基金表现强劲
反映全球乳业市场对原料供应的积极预期
对跨境奶粉供应链有重要影响
body: FSF, NZFSFE0001S5, Illustration mit AI erstellt. Fonterra has raised the midpoint of its 2026/27 farmgate milk price forecast from NZD 9.50 to NZD 9.75 per kilogram of milk solids. The cooperative also narrowed the forecast range to NZD 9.00-NZD 10.50 from NZD 8.50-NZD 10.50. The announcement on Friday, October 30, 2026, strengthens the operating backdrop for Fonterra Shareholders' Fund units, although it does not by itself establish a price reaction. In its official release , Fonterra said the update was driven largely by improving demand for whole milk powder and skim milk powder. Prices for the two products at the latest two Global Dairy Trade events rose by about 5 percent and 7 percent respectively, according to the company. Fonterra attributed the demand improvement to Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Africa and China. The cooperative also cited a well-contracted sales book despite record milk collections, while cautioning that global supply and demand could still affect the outlook. The organic milk price forecast was lifted as well. Its midpoint rose from NZD 14.30 to NZD 15.25 per kilogram of milk solids, while the range moved to NZD 14.50-NZD 16.00 from NZD 13.30-NZD 15.30. The higher milk price outlook can improve the earnings environment for farmer suppliers and supports the broader value proposition behind the fund units. Investors still face exposure to dairy commodity prices, production volumes, currency movements and demand in major export markets. Fonterra's FY27 earnings guidance remains 65 to 85 cents per share, according to its investor page. Fonterra is a farmer-owned New Zealand dairy cooperative that collects milk and sells milk-derived products through ingredients, consumer and foodservice channels. Its markets include New Zealand, global markets outside Greater China and Greater China itself, according to MarketWatch . The company operates at broad cooperative scale, while Synlait Milk and a2 Milk represent more focused dairy competitors in the New Zealand market.
